sections.heading: Objectives
mechanicsSummary: Each game requires one or more objectives. The number required is printed on the board for that month.
At least one objective is mandatory. Mandatory objectives are required to win.
The group does not have to choose the optional objectives before the game starts.
An objective stays available in later months, even after it has been completed, unless an instruction says to destroy it.

sections.heading: The Dossiers
mechanicsSummary: Some cards carry dossier numbers or letters.
When told to, open the matching precut door on a dossier and tear it off.

sections.heading: The Packages
mechanicsSummary: Open a numbered package only when the game says to.

sections.heading: The Reserve
mechanicsSummary: Box storage for cards, stickers, and pieces that are not in the current game but may be needed during or after one.

sections.heading: Rationed and Unrationed Events
mechanicsSummary: At the start of each game the group chooses Rationed Event cards and adds a number of them equal to the current rationing level.
Rationing starts at 4 for the prologue and for the start of January, then rises and falls. Minimum 0, maximum 10.
Unrationed Event cards are found later. Each is always in the Player deck, ignoring rationing, until it is used. Using one destroys it.

sections.heading: Tracking Tokens
mechanicsSummary: Black tokens mark progress toward the current objectives.

sections.heading: Card Stickers
mechanicsSummary: Some cards have an improvement space. Improvements are applied during the Game End Production step.
A card holds at most one improvement, and only if it has a space.
Infection-card improvements and City-card improvements have different shapes so they are not swapped.
Pictured Infrastructure improvement: that card counts as 3 cards of its color when building a supply center.
Pictured Well Stocked improvement: if the city already has 2 or more supply cubes when this Infection card is drawn, remove no supply cubes.

sections.heading: Turning Point Cards
mechanicsSummary: Every Turning Point card found is stored in the reserve, then moved to the Game End area at the start of each game.
At game end, check whether its requirement was met. If yes, follow the card. If no, return it to the reserve for the next game.
None are in play at the start of the campaign. They appear as the year continues.

sections.heading: Supply Cubes
mechanicsSummary: Gray cubes. They are what keeps a city from the plague.
When an Infection card is drawn, move 1 supply cube from that city to the stockpile.
If the city has no supply cube when the card is drawn, place a plague cube instead.

sections.heading: Plague Cubes
mechanicsSummary: Green cubes. No cure or treatment is known.

sections.heading: Supply Centers
mechanicsSummary: Temporary structures built during a game (hospital, depot, and headquarters combined).
They do not persist between games. The Hollow Men tear them down.
A city with a supply center may play Produce Supplies cards.
At the end of a game, each city that has a supply center gains population.

sections.heading: Produce Supply Cards
mechanicsSummary: Always shuffled into the Player deck.
Played at a haven or supply center to produce many supplies in one turn. The action is on page 10.
